answerability: partly: the data can compare the motorist/cyclist composition of recorded deaths by crash year, but it cannot compare death risk without exposure data.
metric: For each year, motorist deaths and cyclist deaths as percentages of the sum of the two recorded death totals.
denominator: For each year, the sum of recorded motorist and cyclist deaths; the two class shares sum to 100% when the denominator is positive.
population: All police-reported NYC motor vehicle crashes dated 2013-01-01 through 2025-12-31; death totals sum the respective crash-level killed counts.
years: 2013-2025 inclusive, grouped by calendar year of crash_date.
grouping: Calendar year and road-user class (motorist, cyclist).
data_check_findings: The plan population contains 2,132,218 crash rows; per-year row counts are in check_2.csv. There are 0 rows with missing crash_date before the year filter, 0 missing motorist killed values, and 0 missing cyclist killed values in 2013-2025. Each target year has rows spanning January 1 through December 31, and none of its rows have the candidate 1970-01-01 date sentinel.
data_check_decision: No plan change. Keep all in-range rows; no rows are dropped or counted differently for missing date or killed-count values. The date range boundaries are represented, though boundary presence alone does not establish completeness of reporting on every date.
missing_outcome_handling: Sum the recorded crash-level killed counts; no values are missing in the planned population, so no rows or outcome values are omitted.
limitations: Shares describe only the composition of recorded motorist and cyclist deaths; they exclude pedestrian deaths and do not measure either group's death risk. The file has no travel, population, or other exposure denominator. The checked date boundaries are present for every year, but that does not prove complete reporting on every date.
